RagShortTexts: In 374 AD, Angles governed from Southern Jutland (Angeln), under the paramount rule of Anglian Sea-Kings.
The polity asserted sovereign legitimacy anchored in Angles dynastic heritage and royal assemblies.
Surrounded by shifting imperial and tribal pressures, the regime enforced loyalty through binding oaths and martial law.

Variants.Content: In 374 AD, the sovereign authority of Angles anchored itself within Southern Jutland (Angeln), confronting the accelerating tremors of Late Antiquity. Governed by Anglian Sea-Kings, the state projected imperial legitimacy through dynastic lineage, military patronage, and strict codification of feudal oaths. Emphasizing institutional doctrine rooted in Angles heritage, the crown mobilized loyal retinues and aristocratic councils to repel external encroachment. Beneath ceremonial grandeur lay unceasing vigilance against shifting steppe incursions and frontier uprisings, compelling the leadership to bind provincial magnates to the throne through land redistribution and martial alliance, safeguarding royal continuity amid an era of continent-wide transition.

Sea-king's warriors swear their oaths by the banner at dusk, repeating each line after the priest. Their sergeant tells them that when the Anglian war standards move, every man must wear iron armor and carry his shield to the front. The promise of gold and land keeps them steady, though a few wonder whether the king will remember them after the battle.

The sea-king's reeve reports that several coastal clans refuse to honor the royal writs until their old rights to the ferries are confirmed. Invite the clan chiefs to a private meeting and offer to reaffirm their ferry tolls in exchange for their oaths. Do not seal any such promise in the king's name, because the chancellor will treat it as an unauthorized grant.
